question: Among Hebrew operators already covered by a pre-glyph Song functional registry, which independently frozen annotation map—Song function groups, conventional OSHB morphology, or blind Hebrew structural clusters—predicts organization among their independently matched glyph operators?
claimBoundary: A winning map predicts relational organization of glyph operator behavior on the frozen Song-covered Hebrew panel. It does not establish translation, lexical equivalence, historical contact, common authorship, theology, phonetics, physical machine execution, or that a glyph carries an English gloss.

hebrewSource.tokenIdentity: first numeric lemma component rendered H<number>

commonPanel.selection: union of Strong IDs explicitly present in the frozen Song group manifest, then exact-V15 train support/coverage/norm gates; no Hebrew frequency-rank cap is applied to the Song-covered panel
commonPanel.pairing: label-blind deterministic global-greedy one-to-one assignment maximizing train weighted-cosine Hebrew↔glyph fingerprint similarity

song.relation: two panel operators are related when they share at least one explicitly frozen Song group

conventional.source: OSHB morphology on Hebrew TRAIN occurrences only
conventional.targetMorphAlignment: split lemma and morph fields on slash; use the morph segment aligned to the first numeric lemma component
conventional.coarseFamily: after optional H language prefix, N/V/A/P/T/S families keep first two characters; other families keep first character
conventional.relation: two panel operators are related when their train-derived coarse morphology-family sets overlap

blind.source: Hebrew TRAIN exact-V15 fingerprint vectors only
blind.kSelection: highest mean silhouette on Hebrew train; ties choose smaller K

evaluation.mapPrimaryMetric: operator-balanced leave-one-operator-out advantage: for each operator, mean glyph similarity to annotation-related partners minus mean similarity to unrelated partners; average across operators having both
evaluation.mapSecondaryMetric: pairwise mean glyph similarity among annotation-related pairs minus unrelated pairs
evaluation.null: permute whole annotation bundles/cluster labels across the fixed Hebrew panel; this preserves each map's category topology and label multiplicities while breaking alignment to the frozen glyph partners
evaluation.fullRule: the label-blind Hebrew↔glyph common-panel pairing must pass both reused lanes before annotation-map results are interpreted; each annotation map must independently pass its map gate in both lanes
